CLINICAL FEATURES OF MICRONUTRIENT DEFICIENCIES
Clinical Features
- Iron: anaemia
- Iodine: goitre
- Zinc, copper: manifestations of enzyme and insulin deficiencies
- Calcium: rickets, osteomalacia
- Phosphorus and fluoride: teeth and bone abnormalities
- Vitamins:
- A: keratomalacia, corneal xerosis, night blindness
- B1 (thiamine): beri-beri
- B2(riboflavin): scrotal and vulval dermatoses, angular stomatitis, scars,
Magenta tongue, cheilosis
- B3 (niacin): scarlet and dry tongue, pellagra
- C (Ascorbic acid): scurvy, petechiae and musculo-skeletal
haemorrhages
- D: rickets, epiphyseal enlargement, muscle wasting, bossing of skull
bone, 'thoracic rosary', persistently open anterior fontanelle, genu
valgum or varum
Investigations
- Blood, urine and stool tests. Other Investigations as appropriate
